name: Netflix
summary: Netflix interviews lean heavily on its culture memo, which it publishes on its careers site and which names values such as Judgment, Candor, Courage and Selflessness. Its new-grad page says candidates may be asked which parts of the memo resonate with them, or don't, and candidates commonly report culture-focused conversations alongside technical or functional interviews.
rounds: Interviews on the culture: judgement, candor and how you work
looks_for: Candor: giving and taking direct feedback
Selflessness: taking time to help others succeed
Inclusion: recognising your biases and working against them

questions.text: Tell me about a time you gave someone difficult feedback.
covers: Why the feedback needed giving and why it was hard
How you gave it: specific, timely, aimed at helping them
What changed, and how the relationship held up

questions.text: Tell me about a decision you made without asking for permission. How did it go?
covers: The context you had and why you felt able to decide
Who you informed and how you managed the risk
The outcome, good or bad, and what you'd do next time

questions.text: What feedback have you received that changed how you work?
covers: The feedback itself, stated honestly
What you changed in your behaviour
Evidence the change stuck

questions.text: Tell me about a time you made an important call with incomplete information.
covers: What you knew, what you didn't, and the cost of waiting
How you weighed the options and whose views you sought
The result and how you'd judge the decision now

questions.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision, said so, and then committed to it.
covers: Your view and how you voiced it
Why the decision went the other way
How you fully supported it afterwards, and what happened

questions.text: Tell me about a risk you took that didn't work out.
covers: Why the risk was worth taking at the time
What went wrong and how you responded
What you learned, and whether you'd take a similar risk again

questions.text: Tell me about a time you put the team's goal ahead of your own.
covers: What you wanted and what the team needed
What you gave up or took on
The result for the team

questions.text: How would you design a system that recommends what someone should watch next?
covers: Signals: viewing history, ratings, time of day, what similar members watch
Candidate generation then ranking, and handling new members and new titles
How you'd measure success beyond clicks, such as finishing what they start

questions.text: How would you design video streaming so playback starts quickly and adapts to a weak connection?
covers: Encoding each title at several qualities and splitting it into short chunks
The player choosing quality chunk by chunk, with caches close to viewers
Measuring start time, rebuffering and picture quality

questions.text: How would you test a change to the home page with members before rolling it out to everyone?
covers: An A/B test with a clear main metric and guardrails
Sample size, test length and splitting by device or region
How you'd decide when results are mixed

questions.text: How would you keep a service available when one of the services it depends on starts failing?
covers: Timeouts, retries with backoff, and circuit breakers
Fallbacks that degrade gracefully, such as cached or default results
Testing failure on purpose before it happens for real

questions.text: Which part of the Netflix culture memo resonates with you most, and which would you find hardest?
covers: A specific part of the memo, named accurately
An example from your own work that shows it
An honest answer about the hard part and how you'd handle it

questions.text: Why Netflix, and why this role now?
covers: What draws you to the team's work and to Netflix's way of working
Why this is the right step in your career now
What you'd contribute in the first months

questions.text: What would you want to know about how this team works before deciding to join?
covers: Questions about how decisions and feedback work on the team
What great performance looks like in the role
Questions that show you've read the culture memo

tips: Read the Netflix culture memo before the interview.
Be direct and specific; they value candor over polish.
Form a view on parts of the memo such as the keeper test and 'disagree then commit'; interviewers may ask what you think.
Netflix's new-grad page says that process typically includes a take-home assessment and two rounds of interviews; experienced roles vary, so ask your recruiter.
When you describe a decision, give the context you had, the call you made, and how you'd decide again.
